records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Parts of a Sentence (Q1)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Parts of a Sentence; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Parts of a Sentence.

content.prompt: Identify the subject in: “The young athlete won the race.”

answer.explanation: The subject tells who or what the sentence is about: “The young athlete.”

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Parts of a Sentence (Q2)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Parts of a Sentence; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Parts of a Sentence.

content.prompt: Identify the predicate in: “Our teacher explained the lesson clearly.”

answer.explanation: The predicate states what the subject does or what is said about it.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Parts of a Sentence (Q3)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Parts of a Sentence; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Parts of a Sentence.

content.prompt: Which sentence has an imperative form?

answer.explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command, request, instruction, or advice.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Verbs (Q4)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Verbs; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Verbs.

content.prompt: Choose the main verb: “The children were playing outside.”

answer.explanation: “Playing” is the main action verb; “were” is the helping verb.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Verbs (Q5)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Verbs; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Verbs.

content.prompt: Choose the correct verb: “Each of the players ___ a water bottle.”

answer.explanation: “Each” is singular, so the verb takes the singular form “has.”

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Verbs (Q6)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Verbs; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Verbs.

content.prompt: Which sentence uses a linking verb?

answer.explanation: “Smells” links the subject “soup” to the description “delicious.”

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Time and Tense (Q7)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Time and Tense; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Time and Tense.

content.prompt: Choose the correct form: “Mina ___ to school every day.”

answer.explanation: The simple present describes a routine; the third-person singular subject “Mina” takes “walks.”

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Time and Tense (Q8)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Time and Tense; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Time and Tense.

content.prompt: Complete the sentence: “We ___ the museum yesterday.”

answer.explanation: “Yesterday” indicates a finished past action, so use the simple past “visited.”

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Time and Tense (Q9)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Time and Tense; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Time and Tense.

content.prompt: Choose the correct form: “I ___ my homework, so I can go out now.”

answer.explanation: The present perfect connects a completed action with the present result.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Time and Tense (Q10)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Time and Tense; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Time and Tense.

content.prompt: Complete the sentence: “At 8 p.m. last night, they ___ dinner.”

answer.explanation: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a particular time in the past.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Parts of a Sentence (Q11)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Parts of a Sentence; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Parts of a Sentence.

answer.explanation: “The bus arrived late” expresses a complete thought with a subject and predicate.

records.subject: English (SLE)
records.title: Original practice: Verbs (Q12)
records.sourceReference: Syllabus topic: Verbs; official Class IX HSC SLE syllabus 2026–27. The question itself is original practice content.
records.learningOutcome: Apply the Class IX English syllabus skill: Verbs.

content.prompt: Choose the correct verb: “Neither the captain nor the players ___ ready.”

answer.explanation: With “neither…nor,” the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject; “players” is plural, so use “are.”
